J U D G M E N T :

1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present appeal, challenging the order dated 23.08.2018 ("the impugned order" in short) of Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (North),
Alipur, Delhi ("ADM" in short), whereby he imposed FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 1 of 9 penalty of Rs.60,000/ (Rupees sixty thousand only) upon the appellant under Section 54 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short), for selling food article i.e. Milk Cake containing extraneous matter in contravention to Section 26(2)(ii) & 27(1) of FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(i) of FSS Act, 2006.
2.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 1 of 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Briefly stating, the facts as per the appeal are that appellant is running a shop under the name &
style of M/s Yadav Misthan Bhandar at Shop No. 407, Phatakwali Gali,Village Bhorgarh, Delhi40.

On 28.04.2016, a sample of "Milk Cake" was lifted by the Food Safety Officer (in short FSO) from the aforesaid premises where the sampled commodity was found stored for sale and the appellant was found vending the sampled commodity at the time of taking the sample.

On analysis, the Food Analyst, Delhi, vide its report dated 04.05.2016, opined the said sample to be containing extraneous matter viz. added vegetable oil and added starch in contravention of Section 26(2)(ii) read with the definition of extraneous matter as defined under Section 3(1)(i) of the FSS Act.

Consequently, a Sh. Trilok Yadav S/O Sh. Dukhaa Yadav vs Food Safety Officer on 18 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65545514/
1 complaint was filed against the appellantherein by the FSO before the Adjudicating Officer.

sentences.text: After pleadings and enquiry, the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order dated 23.08.2018 imposing a penalty of Rs.60,000/ upon the appellant.

3. The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 2 of 9 alia on the grounds among others that the appellant has not been granted sufficient time to represent his case before the Ld. ADM.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 2 of 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant is running only a Tea shop from the said premises and not indulging in making any kind of sweets in his shop.
Appellant used to sell sweets only after purchasing the same from other shop namely Jain Sweets, Narela, Delhi40.
Appellant was not afforded with fair opportunity to put his defence before the Ld. ADM as he was directly served with the recovery notices dated 01.11.2018 & 01.03.2019.
The Ld. ADM deliberately not served the appellant with the impugned order dated 23.08.2018.
The proceedings conducted before the Ld. ADM is without the principle of natural justice as no opportunity of hearing was granted to the appellant.
4. The Ld. Chief PP for the State has not filed reply to the appeal, however, he has opposed the appeal.

5. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the appellant and Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State and have perused the records and also gone through the judgment relied upon by the Ld. Chief PP for the State.
6. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that impugned order in this case was passed on 23.08.2018 whereas the appellant has received the notice on 01.04.2019.
No notice was given to the appellant.
On 17.04.2018, the appellant appeared and filed reply to FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 3 of 9 the said notice.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the same day i.e. on 17.04.2018, he was informed about the passing of the impugned order.
Sweets were packed and not opened.
Nothing is brought on record that the appellant was preparing the sweets from the shop.
Appellant was not given the opportunity to lead evidence in support of his case.
No further notice was issued and received by the appellant after 17.04.2018.
No time of raid is mentioned.

Nothing is mentioned whether any person or public witness was available or not for joining the proceedings by the FSO.
7.
The Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor argued that the appellant was having full opportunity to lead evidence but he did not appear before the Ld. ADM.
The appellant endorsed that the sampled commodity was prepared at his shop.
The appellant nowhere denied that the sampled commodity does not belong to him.

Appellant is the owner of the said shop i.e. M/s Yadav Misthan Bhandar and was found selling the sampled commodity containing extraneous matter as per the report of Food Analyst, therefore, he is liable as per Section 27 of FSS Act.
The appellant did not comply with the standards of rules / regulations of Food Safety and Standard Act.
The impugned order has been rightly passed by the Ld.ADM.

The Ld. Chief PP for the State, in support of his arguments, relied upon the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar versus The State of Uttar FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 4 of 9 Pradesh in Criminal Appeal No. 1541 of 2019 decided on 04.10.2019 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

In the present case, the appellant has challenged the impugned order dt.23.08.2018 mainly on the grounds that no proper opportunity of hearing was given to him by the Ld. ADM before passing the impugned order and that he was not even served with the impugned order.
The Ld. ADM directly sent him with the recovery notices dated 01.11.2018 & 01.03.2019.

Ld. ADM has failed to appreciate that appellant has purchased/bought the sweets from other shop namely Jain Sweets,
Narela and therefore, he is not liable.

9. The Food Analyst vide his report dated 04.05.2016 opined the sample to be containing extraneous matter viz. added vegetable oil and added starch in contravention of Section 26(2)(ii) read with the definition of extraneous matter as defined under Section 3(1)(i) of the FSS Act.
10. Section 3(1)(i) FSS Act defines "extraneous matter".

It reads as under :
Section 3 : Definition (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires ....
(i) "extraneous matter" means any matter contained in an article of FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 5 of 9 food which may be carried from the raw materials, packaging materials or process systems used for its manufacture or which is added to it, but such matter does not render such article of food unsafe;
11.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears from the above relevant provisions that the added vegetable oil and added starch which was added to the Milk Cake, is covered under the definition of 'extraneous matter'.

However,
it needs to be read and considered in conjunction with Section 26(2)(ii) FSS Act, for violation of which, the appellant has been penalised.
12. Section 26(2)(ii) FSS Act casts a responsibility on FBO not to manufacture, store, sell or distribute food article containing extraneous matter.

Said provision reads as under:
26.Responsibilities of the Food business operator.

....
(2) No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food - .....
(ii)which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter; or"
13.
Section 27(1) FSS Act fastens liability for sale etc. of food article upon the manufacture or packer.
Said provision reads as under: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 6 of 9 "27. Liability of the Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 6 of 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(1)The manufacturer or packer of an article of food shall be liable for such article of food if it does not meet the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder."
Sh. Trilok Yadav S/O Sh. Dukhaa Yadav vs Food Safety Officer on 18 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65545514/
3 14.

entities.text: Dukhaa Yadav vs Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above provisions of law, the manufacturer or packer / appellant is liable for manufacturing/selling/supply of sampled food article containing extraneous matter.
15. It is pertinent to mention here that Form VA mentioned that the "Milk Cake is prepared from Milk Sugar & Pista pieces, as disclosed by FBO".
The said Form VA as well as the Panchnama was duly signed by the appellant which shows that the sampled commodity was lifted from the spot in the presence of appellant on 28.04.2016.

The appellant did not mention anywhere in the proceedings (Form VANotice to the FBO, Panchnama and Raid report) conducted by the FSO while lifting the said sample that he had purchased the sampled commodity from Jain Sweets, as alleged by him in the present appeal filed before this court.

The appellant is the FBOcum proprietor/owner of M/s Yadav Misthan Bhandar and he looks after its daytoday business and therefore, he is the In charge of and responsible for the conduct of its business.
FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 7 of 9 16.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 7 of 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant did not make any request to the FSO to send the sample for analysis from an NABL Accredited Laboratory.

The Designated Officer sent a copy of the Food Analyst report to the appellant on 05.05.2016 for giving him opportunity to file an appeal against the Food Analyst's report dated 04.05.2016 for sending one counterpart of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory but no such appeal was preferred by the appellant in this regard.
17. The record of the Ld. ADM reveals that hearings of the case were held on different dates but the appellant has failed to appear on those dates of hearings except on 17.04.2018.
As the appellant had failed to appear despite service of notices, the Ld. ADM heard the matter exparte on 27.07.2018 and thereafter, passed the impugned order on 23.08.2018.
Notices dated 01.11.2018 and 01.03.2019 were also issued to the appellant for recovery of the penalty amount of Rs.60,000/.
The record of the Ld. ADM further reveals that several opportunities were given to the appellant to appear and put up his defence in support of his case.

However, notices dated 20.06.2017, 03.11.2017, 05.12.2017, 31.05.2018 sent to the appellant FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 8 of 9 through Speed Post received back with the report that the addressee is not residing at the given address.

entities.text: FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is evident that sufficient opportunities were afforded to the appellant to put up his defence/case but he neither appeared nor defended his case before the Ld. ADM, the reasons are best known to him.

18. In view of the above facts and circumstances, arguments on behalf of the parties and the materials available on reocrd and also the judgments relied upon by the Ld. Chief PP for the State, I am of the considered opinion that there is no infirmity in the impugned order dated 23.08.2018 of the Ld. ADM.
The parameters and standards laid down by the legislatures were not followed by the appellant for selling the Milk Cake.
Thus, the appellant has failed to demonstrate any justified reason to interfere with the said impugned order of the Ld. ADM.
Section 54 of FSS Act prescribes a maximum penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ (Rupees One Lac only).
The Ld. ADM imposed a penalty of Rs.60,000 lacs upon the appellant.

Accordingly, this appeal is devoid of any merits and the same is Sh. Trilok Yadav S/O Sh. Dukhaa Yadav vs Food Safety Officer on 18 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65545514/
4 dismissed.
